newsitem.title: USA: House, Senate budget writers hold conference.
newsitem.headline: House, Senate budget writers hold conference.

text.p: House and Senate budget writers said Tuesday they would file a joint report on the five-year balanced budget plan so both chambers can vote on the hard-fought deal later this week without amendments.

Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici held the brief session to fill a requirement for a public meeting as part of the process of settling differences between the House and Senate versions of the budget plan.
Substantive differences between the bills had been worked out previously, and just a few technical items remained, the New Mexico Republican said.
"All the work's been done, but unless we put it into a conference report, it would have been amendable," Domenici said.
Lawmakers hoped to avoid any last-minute snags with the budget plans and hold quick final votes in both chambers Thursday.
The plan calls for a net $85 billion in tax cuts over the next five years, $115 billion in Medicare cuts over five years and a slower rate of growth for other government programmes.
